subject: Renewal pricing: anchored uptick with flex-credit bridge
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@seaedge.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing: anchored uptick with flex-credit bridge

Hi Elena —

Hope you had a good week. SeaEdge's initial renewal window is coming up in August and I wanted to start the pricing conversation early so we have time to land a structure that supports your expected 35% Q4 uptick without surprising cost volatility.

High-level idea I sketched: a 12-month renewal with a two-tranche commit (Base + Upside buffer). We anchor pricing on current committed rates for the Base tranche, and introduce a flex-credit bridge that:
- provides discounted capacity for burst usage above the Base (applies as credits that offset overage tokens),
- preserves predictable unit pricing for committed capacity, and
- phases credit unwind across three milestones tied to monthly throughput.

This would let SeaEdge absorb the Q4 increase with a known budget path while Redwood preserves margin on steady-state usage. I can share a short spreadsheet and an updated proposal that quantifies dollar impact and breakpoints.

Are you available for a 30-minute sync next week? If procurement wants to join, happy to include them — we typically include a short MA that lists credit triggers and an ops SLA addendum.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber

Jonas —

Thanks for the early outreach. Our finance lead is conservative on fixed commits but we need elasticity for the Q4 launch. Procurement (cc'd) prefers a simple commit + a timebound credit pool vs complicated step functions.

Key asks from SeaEdge:
1) Show net dollar impact at current run-rate + 35% burst scenario (monthly view).
2) Limit the credit pool to a predictable cap and spell out carry-forward rules.
3) Include an option to convert unused credits into a one-time invoice credit at year-end (not automatic roll-forward).

If you can get a one-pager and the numbers, procurement will take a look quickly. We can meet Wed 6/16 10:00 PT if that works for you and your pricing lead.

Elena

Subject: Proposed renewal & flex-credit bridge (SeaEdge AI) — proposal attached

Elena / SeaEdge team —

Following up with an updated proposal PDF and a short table showing monthly spend at three scenarios: Current run-rate, +20% seasonal, +35% launch burst. Key bullets:
- 12-month term with a Base commit that mirrors current unit pricing for committed capacity.
- Upside buffer (Flex Credit Pool): capped at 20% of Base commit monthly. Credits apply as dollar offsets to overage invoices and expire at contract year-end.
- Conversion option: Customer may elect one-time conversion of up to 50% of unused credits into a pre-approved invoice credit at year-end (conversion rate defined in section 3).
- SLA credits remain separate and will not exhaust Flex Credits.
- Can offer 10% one-time onboarding credit if SeaEdge signs by 7/15 to help cover migration testing.

Attached: SeaEdge_MAProposal_v2.pdf (proposal with tables)
Attached: usage-telemetry-2026.csv (monthly token counts)

Please review and let me know if procurement needs alternative language — happy to walk through during the Wed 10:00 PT call.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement has two redlines before we escalate to legal: 
1) Need explicit language that unused credits cannot be assigned or sold; conversion option requires a signed request before 12/31.
2) Request a cap on the total dollar value of credits per quarter (we suggest a hard cap at 25% of quarterly Base spend to avoid runaway one-off reductions).

If you can accept those items, Procurement will draft the commercial redlines and we can move to DocuSign. Also confirm the onboarding credit mechanics (10% applied as a credit on first invoice vs. direct credit note).

We can join a short call tomorrow if needed.

Procurement
